in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Thank you for your inquiry about Child Benefit. Based on the information provided about your situation, I need to assess your eligibility.

You've indicated you live in the UK and are asking about Child Benefit for Alex, who is 21 years old and lives with you.

Let me review the key eligibility rules:

**Age Requirements:**
- Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16
- It can continue for children aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training
- The benefit stops at age 20 (even if in approved education/training)

**Work and Benefits:**
- Child Benefit stops if the child starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training
- Child Benefit stops if the child starts getting certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit

**Your Situation with Alex:**
Alex is 21 years old, which exceeds the maximum age limit of 20 for Child Benefit eligibility. Additionally, Alex works 24+ hours per week, is not in approved education, and receives qualifying benefits (UC or ESA) in their own right.

## My Assessment

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

There are actually three separate reasons why Alex does not qualify:

1. **Age**: Alex is 21 years old. Child Benefit only covers children up to age 16, or up to age 20 if they remain in approved education or training. At 21, Alex has exceeded the maximum age limit.

2. **Employment status**: Alex works 24 or more hours per week and is not in approved education or training. This alone would end Child Benefit eligibility.

3. **Benefits in own right**: Alex receives qualifying benefits (such as Universal Credit or ESA) in their own right. When a child starts receiving these types of benefits themselves, Child Benefit stops.

Any one of these factors would be enough to make Alex ineligible, but in your case, all three apply.

If you have any questions about this decision or need clarification about the rules, please feel free to ask.
